“By fluent we mean students can recall facts without hesitation and can perform routine calculations without thought–similar to speaking a language fluently.” (Source: Fluency without Equivocation by Scott Baldridge, Ben McCarthy, and Robin Ramos)

“Fluency is designed to promote automaticity by engaging students in practice in ways that get their adrenaline flowing. Automaticity is critical so that students avoid using up too many of their attention resources with lower-level skills when they are addressing higher-level problems. The automaticity prepares students with the computational foundation to enable deep understanding in flexible ways.” (Source: Fluency without Equivocation by Scott Baldridge, Ben McCarthy, and Robin Ramos)
Fluency is not taught in a fixed number of instructional periods; it should be practiced and maintained throughout the school year.
